title: Command: undo, redo, replays
summary: Turn every action into an object.

cards.title: Actions as objects
cards.body:
Instead of `movePlayer(1, 0)`, create a `MoveCommand(1, 0)` object and call `execute()`. Because the action is now **data**, you can store it, undo it, replay it, send it over the network, or remap which button creates it.

Undo needs each command to remember enough to reverse itself.
Watch the two stacks: undo and redo. Step 8 is the subtle rule.
Commands are owned by `std::unique_ptr` and **moved** between the stacks: exactly the ownership model from the smart-pointer lesson.

cards.question: You undo twice, then make a new move. What happens to the redo stack?
cards.explain: The new move starts a different future; the old redo history no longer makes sense, so it's cleared. Every editor works this way.
